chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade that the meat of the sacrifices be kept for more than three days. This does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that Muḥammad ibn Muslim shared with Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ in hearing the report, and that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade that, then later said: then he permitted after that its consumption. Muḥammad ibn Muslim forgot it, while Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated it. And even if it were accepted as it stands, it would be permissible to interpret it as a type of recommendation, because what remains after three days is better to be given in charity.

key_terms.النَّبِيَّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as the source of the ruling
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ الْأَوَّلِ: the earlier report mentioned for comparison
key_terms.لُحُومُ الْأَضَاحِيِّ: the meat of sacrificial animals offered on the prescribed occasion
key_terms.يُتَصَدَّقَ بِهِ: to give it away in charity

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat of sacrificial animals after three days in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on keeping and eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days. It explains that the apparent prohibition does not necessarily conflict with other reports, either because a later permission abrogated it or because the earlier prohibition may be understood as recommending charity with the remaining meat.
